examples.label: Show why a host is up/down
Disable ARP ping (force ICMP on LAN)

notes: `-sn` = host discovery only (no port scan). `-PE` forces ICMP echo. On a filtered host add `-Pn` to skip discovery and scan anyway.

references.title: HTB Academy - Network Enumeration with Nmap

name: Nmap - Single-Host Discovery with ICMP
description: Probe one host for liveness. -PE forces an ICMP echo request; --packet-trace shows every packet; --disable-arp-ping stops Nmap short-circuiting via ARP on the local segment.

defense.why_it_works: Nmap sends ICMP echo requests, TCP SYN/ACK probes, and ARP requests to determine if a single target host is alive. Even without port scanning, host discovery reveals which systems are reachable — a prerequisite for scoping further enumeration and lateral movement. [MITRE T1018] Adversaries use remote system discovery to map the network and identify hosts for lateral movement.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to the target address.
defense.impact: Confirmation that a specific host is alive before committing to a full port scan.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1018 AN1583] Execution of network enumeration utilities (ping, nmap -sn) against a target, particularly when followed by deeper port scanning or exploitation. Single-host ICMP probes are lower fidelity but still logged by network monitoring tools.
defense.artifacts: ICMP echo, ARP, and TCP SYN/ACK probes to the target in firewall/IDS logs.
defense.prevention: Firewall rules that drop ICMP echo and unsolicited probes make a host appear inactive to default discovery (HTB M03: hosts ignoring ICMP are marked down). This only defeats ICMP-based discovery — on the local segment ARP still reveals live hosts — so network segmentation and NAC matter more than ICMP filtering alone.
defense.evasion: On a local segment Nmap falls back to ARP, which reveals hosts even when ICMP is firewalled; vary probe types (-PS/-PA/-PU) to find hosts that ignore default ICMP echo, and slow the timing to stay quiet.
defense.misconfiguration: Network perimeters that do not filter ICMP, do not use egress filtering, or expose unnecessary services (all ports open) allow comprehensive port scanning. Systems without host-based firewalls or IDS/IPS allow scan traffic to enumerate every open service, revealing attack surface. No rate-limiting on inbound probes means stealth scans complete quickly.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# No firewall between attacker and target (or overly permissive rules):
# iptables -L  ->  Chain INPUT (policy ACCEPT)  [no rules]
# Or: Windows Firewall disabled
# Every service's port is reachable from any source

# No IDS/IPS:
# Snort/Suricata not deployed; no AWS GuardDuty / Azure Defender
# Nmap SYN scan completes in seconds with no alert generated
defense.secure_config:
# Linux host-based firewall — default-deny inbound:
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
# Only open required services:
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT  # HTTPS only
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -s 10.10.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT  # SSH from mgmt network

# Rate-limit scan detection (drops SYN floods):
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -m limit --limit 1/s --limit-burst 3 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -j DROP

# Deploy IDS/IPS:
# Snort/Suricata rules detect nmap OS detection probes
# AWS: GuardDuty (detects port scans from EC2)
# Cloud: Security Groups default-deny with explicit allow rules
